a bullish order block is typically the last bearish candle before a powerful upward move that breaks structure

price retraces downward and forms a change of character by breaking an internal low. This change of character does not signal a trend reversal, but rather a temporary internal shift. During this retracement, price returns into the bullish order block and fills the buy orders resting inside the zone
the change of character acted as an entry trigger rather than a reversal signal
In a bullish order block, a buy limit order is placed at the level of the upper wick of the candle that defines the order block boundaries

The first and most powerful confirmation of a valid order block is the liquidity sweep, also known as the takeout... The final bearish candle breaks the low of the previous candle and immediately reverses upward. This move, taking out the prior low, is the liquidity sweep

The second key confirmation of a valid order block is the presence of imbalance, also known as inefficiency. Immediately after the liquidity sweep, price should reverse aggressively and move upward with clear impulsive strength... On the chart, this imbalance appears as a fair value gap, an area where one or more candles do not overlap each other

if no imbalance forms above this candle... we do not define the order block based on the liquidity sweep candle. Instead, we extend the order block boundaries to include the next candle. When we analyze that next candle, we can clearly see imbalance forming above it

The third and final confirmation of a valid order block is that it must remain unmitigated. This means that after the order block is formed, price has not yet returned to this zone to retest it or trade through it
